propositions: A transient git fetch hang from the GitHub mirror times out after 300s, raising SnapshotFetchError that is caught as a generic exception and converted to a BLOCK with -1 vote.
The spurious -1 vote persists in the dedup store, removing the change from backfill re-review eligibility because reconcile filters out changes that already have an LLM-Review vote.
The adapter's blanket exception handler cannot distinguish retryable infrastructure faults (git timeout, connection error) from genuine review conclusions, so all exceptions map to fail-closed BLOCK.
The voter immediately converts any BLOCK decision to a -1 vote POST and dedup row write, with no deferral or retry budget.
The system already handles hung reviews correctly one layer up (app.py, reconcile.py) by abstaining without voting, but the adapter layer is inconsistent and votes fail-closed instead.
A fix must route retryable infrastructure exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) to an ABSTAIN decision that posts no vote and writes no dedup row.
